text:
maria: heads up — I'm seeing a 12-18% p95 latency regression on small-req workloads after the recent continuous-batching change when phase separation is enabled. digging in now.

ajay: ugh. which change specifically? the `separate-prefill-decode` toggle we added last week?

maria: yeah that one. baseline (no separation) -> p95 ~ 210ms. with separation + default policy -> p95 ~ 250ms. mean is roughly unchanged.

sophia: interesting — does this reproduce on both A100 and 4090 nodes? could be kernel selection hitting a slower matmul path for short decodes.

maria: repro on both. profiler snapshot attached (short excerpt):

```
# profiler top ops (separate phases ON)
conv_mm_optim: 38%  (kernel: fp16_quant_mm_v2)
softmax: 22%
kv_cache_copy: 15%
attention_qkv: 10%
others: 15%
```

with separation OFF, `conv_mm_optim` drops to 28% and `kv_cache_copy` to 8%.

tim: that kv cache delta looks suspicious. any extra memcpy when we switch queues between prefill/decode?

maria: yes — current implementation flushes partial KV buffers when moving a request between prefill queue and decode queue. that's to avoid mixing batch layouts, but it causes extra copy + memory pressure which lengthens the short tail.

ajay: might be able to fix by making phase-aware batches share a KV layout when the model/seq_len bin matches. i.e., keep requests pinned to a 'phase-group' but allow shared buffers for identical shape.

sophia: also check batching heuristics — token-budget target might be too aggressive for decode batches leading to tiny prefill batches and lots of tiny decode batches that thrash kernels. what are our token budget defaults?

maria: defaults: prefill_budget=1024 tokens, decode_budget=128 tokens. but with separation, we end up with decode batches often <=8 tokens due to per-request decode pacing, so we hit poor kernel selection.

ajay: proposal: make decode budget adaptive by observed seq distribution. if avg decode tokens < 16 then ramp budget to 256 to allow kernel to pick larger matmul tiling. also change queue policy: prefer forming mixed-phase batches only when layout-compatible, else allow short wait (25ms) for decode to accumulate before dispatch.

maria: ran a quick sim with those heuristics on staging: p95 improved from 250ms -> 218ms, p99 from 420ms -> 360ms. CPU side KV copy time dropped ~40%.

tim: nice. do we have an A/B rollout plan? we should be careful with tail-sensitive customers.

sophia: we can gate behind `phase-aware-batching` feature flag per cluster. rollout steps: canary 10% traffic (low-latency customers omitted) -> monitor p95/p99 + kernel path mix -> if stable, 50% -> 100%. add automatic fallback to legacy batching if p99 increases by >10% over baseline.

ajay: I'll draft the change set: two small changes — (1) adaptive decode token_budget, (2) queue policy tweak: wait up to 25ms for compatible layout or tier into short-wait fast-path. also reuse KV buffers when shape matches.

maria: please include microbenchmarks for small decode lengths and measure `conv_mm_optim` kernel invocation counts. we want to ensure kernel selector doesn't regress on long-context workloads.

infra-bot: deploy-check: staging cluster gpu-3 passed smoke tests (tests/kernel-selection, tests/kv-buffering).

maria: thanks. I'll run a longer 24h soak with a mixed workload (chatty short requests + long generator) and post results. anyone object to merging the flag behind canary?

sophia: go for it. :thumbsup:

ajay: merging PR after adding one more unit test for KV buffer reuse case.

maria: perfect. will follow up with perf graphs and kernel traces once soak finishes.
